card.title: Product-launch week drift
card.author: heron
card.hypothesis: After a curated product launch, DEMO's 1W return is higher than its CAPM expectation.
card.rationale: Attention effects around launches. Counter-argument: launches are scheduled and anticipated.
data_needed: events (product) — curated_event (content_available_at): when the press release is public
card.rule: Indicator of a product event in the last 5 sessions before the origin.
card.success_criterion: Beats the CAPM anchor on CRPS at 5 sessions with grade ≥ C.
references: MacKinlay, A.C. (1997) 'Event studies in economics and finance', Journal of Economic Literature, 35(1), pp. 13–39.

checks.text: Hypothesis has a condition, a direction, a horizon and a comparison
Every data item has a timing rule (when it becomes public)
No full-sample statistics in the rule
Horizons are on the contract grid (5, 21, 63, 126, 252 sessions)
Expected +0.3% is below the MDE at 5 sessions (±1.7%)
checks.detail: Likely undetectable on DEMO alone; consider descriptive-only.
Designed without looking at any ProbCast result for 2021 onwards.

amend_note: Content is immutable after registration; an amendment is a new card and counts as a new trial.
